validation.notes: Repaired recoverToolInvocation in packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts: replayed an interrupted effect_pending call whenever EITHER the persisted call policy OR the current tool declaration said replay:"safe" (`call.replay === "safe" || tool?.replay === "safe"`). It now requires both (`const replaySafe = call.replay === "safe" && tool?.replay === "safe"`) and still requires !cancelled; every other case reads the durable checkpoint and publishes the interrupted outcome without clearing it or invoking the tool. .prale-eval/regression.mjs drives the real module through the read-only .prale-eval/subject.mjs createRecoverySubject helper (checkpoint IO, invocation and outcome publication are observable boundary fakes) and asserts the full matrix: both safe -> ['clear','invoke','effect-complete','publish'] with persisted args {persisted:42} replayed and recovery:true; persisted safe + declaration never, persisted never + declaration safe, persisted safe + absent tool, persisted safe + tool without policy, and neither safe -> exactly ['read','publish'] with the durable checkpoint content 'durable-progress', details {step:2}, isError true, terminate false and the 'external outcome is unknown' marker; both safe while cancelled -> interrupted as well, so cancellation never replays. VM-realm results are normalized to plain host-realm data before node:assert/strict comparison. Negative control was executed: temporarily restoring the `||` fault made the regression exit 1 with AssertionError '4 interrupted-recovery scenario(s) violated the replay safety invariant' (callPolicy=safe/toolDeclaration=never, never/safe, safe/absent, safe/no-policy all observed ['clear','invoke','effect-complete','publish']); the fix was then restored and the same command exits 0. Optional type-level validation (tsc/vitest) was unavailable because the workspace has no node_modules and dependencies must not be installed, so only the Node 24 VM regression was run.
